createEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_createEndpointConfig_200_response.endpointNameByCollectedPathTemplateRuleEnabled
createEndpointConfig_200_response.description: The highest default precedence of endpoint rule is creating endpoint is based on path template. For example, ``` /hospital/1948/patient/291148 /hospital/728/patient/924892 /hospital/47/patient/25978 /hospital/108429/patient/1847 ``` can be considered as `/hospital/{hid}/patient/{pid}` if this rule is enabled. For most of the use cases, this rule should be enabled.

createEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_createEndpointConfig_200_response.endpointNameByFirstPathSegmentRuleEnabled
createEndpointConfig_200_response.description: There are endpoint extraction rules in Instana which take the first path segment from the HTTP request and turn this into an endpoint name. For example, given the following URLs `/users/123/profile` and `/users/123/settings`, the extraction rule will only take the first segment. As a result endpoint name will be `users`. Although this is useful in cases where broad overview of monitoring is required, lot of use cases are more specified. Considering the above example, if this rule is enabled, Instana can't distinguish between `profile` or `settings` as endpoints. For use cases where endpoints has to be monitored at fine granular level, this flag should be set to `false`.

createEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_createEndpointConfig_200_response.rules
createEndpointConfig_200_response.description: Specify custom rule configuration apart from Instana predefined rules. This rule has the highest precedence. This is only available for HTTP endpoints.

createEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_createEndpointConfig_200_response.serviceId
createEndpointConfig_200_response.description: An Instana generated unique identifier for a Service. If specified, the list of results will be filtered for the specified Service ID. Eg: `3feb3dcd206c166ef2b41c707e0cd38d7cd325aa`. One can see the service id from Instana UI by going to a Service page. In the URL, there will be `serviceId=3feb3dcd206c166ef2b41c707e0cd38d7cd325aa`. Alternatively, one can use `Get services` API endpoint to get the service id in `id` parameter.

getEndpointConfig_200_response.description: The highest default precedence of endpoint rule is creating endpoint is based on path template. For example, ``` /hospital/1948/patient/291148 /hospital/728/patient/924892 /hospital/47/patient/25978 /hospital/108429/patient/1847 ``` can be considered as `/hospital/{hid}/patient/{pid}` if this rule is enabled. For most of the use cases, this rule should be enabled.

getEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_getEndpointConfig_200_response.endpointNameByFirstPathSegmentRuleEnabled
getEndpointConfig_200_response.description: There are endpoint extraction rules in Instana which take the first path segment from the HTTP request and turn this into an endpoint name. For example, given the following URLs `/users/123/profile` and `/users/123/settings`, the extraction rule will only take the first segment. As a result endpoint name will be `users`. Although this is useful in cases where broad overview of monitoring is required, lot of use cases are more specified. Considering the above example, if this rule is enabled, Instana can't distinguish between `profile` or `settings` as endpoints. For use cases where endpoints has to be monitored at fine granular level, this flag should be set to `false`.

For example, ``` /hospital/1948/patient/291148 /hospital/728/patient/924892 /hospital/47/patient/25978 /hospital/108429/patient/1847 ``` can be considered as `/hospital/{hid}/patient/{pid}` if this rule is enabled. For most of the use cases, this rule should be enabled.

query_getEndpointConfigs_items.name: instana_query_getEndpointConfigs_items.endpointNameByFirstPathSegmentRuleEnabled
query_getEndpointConfigs_items.description: There are endpoint extraction rules in Instana which take the first path segment from the HTTP request and turn this into an endpoint name. For example, given the following URLs `/users/123/profile` and `/users/123/settings`, the extraction rule will only take the first segment. As a result endpoint name will be `users`. Although this is useful in cases where broad overview of monitoring is required, lot of use cases are more specified. Considering the above example, if this rule is enabled, Instana can't distinguish between `profile` or `settings` as endpoints. For use cases where endpoints has to be monitored at fine granular level, this flag should be set to `false`.

query_getEndpointConfigs_items.name: instana_query_getEndpointConfigs_items.rules

Eg: `3feb3dcd206c166ef2b41c707e0cd38d7cd325aa`. One can see the service id from Instana UI by going to a Service page. In the URL, there will be `serviceId=3feb3dcd206c166ef2b41c707e0cd38d7cd325aa`. query_getEndpointConfigs_items_rules_ite.name: instana_query_getEndpointConfigs_items_rules_items.pathSegments
query_getEndpointConfigs_items_rules_ite.description: A list of path segment matching rules, each defining how a segment of the HTTP path should be matched. Each object in this array represents a segment rule, allowing for fixed segments, dynamic parameters, wildcards, or unsupported segments.  **UNSUPPORTED**: A path segment that is not recognized by the system.  **FIXED**: This type represents a static, unchanging part of the URL path. For example, `/api/{version}/users`, `api` and `users` would be `FIXED` segment.  **PARAMETER**: This type represents a variable part of the URL path, often used to capture specific parameters or IDs that change with each request. For example, `/api/{version}/users`, `version` would be `PARAMETER` segment. `version` can be `v1`, `v2`, `v3` etc.  **MATCH_ALL**: This type represents a wildcard, capturing all remaining segments from this point onward in the URL path. For example, `/api/{version}/users/*` — Matches all paths like `/api/v1/users/123`. `/api/v3/users/456` etc.

updateEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_updateEndpointConfig_200_response.endpointNameByCollectedPathTemplateRuleEnabled
updateEndpointConfig_200_response.description: The highest default precedence of endpoint rule is creating endpoint is based on path template. For example, ``` /hospital/1948/patient/291148 /hospital/728/patient/924892 /hospital/47/patient/25978 /hospital/108429/patient/1847 ``` can be considered as `/hospital/{hid}/patient/{pid}` if this rule is enabled. For most of the use cases, this rule should be enabled.

updateEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_updateEndpointConfig_200_response.endpointNameByFirstPathSegmentRuleEnabled
updateEndpointConfig_200_response.description: There are endpoint extraction rules in Instana which take the first path segment from the HTTP request and turn this into an endpoint name. For example, given the following URLs `/users/123/profile` and `/users/123/settings`, the extraction rule will only take the first segment. As a result endpoint name will be `users`. Although this is useful in cases where broad overview of monitoring is required, lot of use cases are more specified. Considering the above example, if this rule is enabled, Instana can't distinguish between `profile` or `settings` as endpoints. For use cases where endpoints has to be monitored at fine granular level, this flag should be set to `false`.

updateEndpointConfig_200_response.name: instana_updateEndpointConfig_200_response.rules
updateEndpointConfig_200_response.description: Specify custom rule configuration apart from Instana predefined rules. This rule has the highest precedence. This is only available for HTTP endpoints.

updateEndpointConfig_200_response.description: An Instana generated unique identifier for a Service. If specified, the list of results will be filtered for the specified Service ID. Alternatively, one can use `Get services` API endpoint to get the service id in `id` parameter.

ChatMessageTextInput.description: An array of objects that specify channels for which the response is intended. If **channels** are present, the response is intended for a built-in integration and should not be handled by an API client.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.beam_width
LLMParamsInput.description: Specifies the number of beams that are used in beam search decoding. A higher value allows for a more exhaustive search, potentially improving the quality of the output at the cost of computational complexity.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.decoding_method
LLMParamsInput.description: Represents the strategy that is used for picking the tokens during generation of the output text. Possible values include 'greedy' for deterministic generation and 'sample' for stochastic generation.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.include_stop_sequence
LLMParamsInput.description: Pass `false` to omit matched stop sequences from the end of the output text. The default is `true`, meaning that the output ends with the stop sequence text when matched.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.length_penalty
LLMParamsInput.description: It can be used to exponentially increase the likelihood of the text generation terminating once a specified number of tokens have been generated.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.max_new_tokens
LLMParamsInput.description: The maximum number of new tokens to be generated. It limits the length of the generated output, preventing it from exceeding a specified size.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.min_new_tokens
LLMParamsInput.description: If stop sequences are given, they are ignored until minimum tokens are generated. The minimum number of new tokens to be generated.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.random_seed
LLMParamsInput.description: Random number generator seed to use in sampling mode for experimental repeatability.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.repetition_penalty
LLMParamsInput.description: Represents the penalty for penalizing tokens that have already been generated or belong to the context. The value 1.0 means that there is no penalty.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.stop_sequences
LLMParamsInput.description: Stop sequences are one or more strings which will cause the text generation to stop if/when they are produced as part of the output.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.temperature
LLMParamsInput.description: A value used to modify the next-token probabilities in sampling mode. Values less than 1.0 sharpen the probability distribution, resulting in \"less random\" output. Values greater than 1.0 flatten the probability distribution, resulting in \"more random\" output. A value of 1.0 has no effect.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.time_limit
LLMParamsInput.description: Time limit in milliseconds - if not completed within this time, generation stops. The text generated so far is returned along with the TIME_LIMIT stop reason.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.top_k
LLMParamsInput.description: The number of highest probability vocabulary tokens to keep for top-k-filtering. Only applies for sampling mode. When decoding_strategy is set to sample, only the top_k most likely tokens are considered as candidates for the next generated token.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.top_p
LLMParamsInput.description: Similar to top_k except the candidates to generate the next token are the most likely tokens with probabilities that add up to at least top_p. Also known as nucleus sampling. A value of 1.0 is equivalent to disabled.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.truncate_input_tokens
LLMParamsInput.description: Truncates the input to a specified number of tokens to prevent exceeding token limits, which may cause request failures.

LLMParamsInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LLMParamsInput.typical_p
LLMParamsInput.description: Measures typicality to control how predictable the next token is compared to the expected randomness. Lower values lead to more diverse outputs.

LengthPenaltyInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LengthPenaltyInput.decay_factor
LengthPenaltyInput.description: Represents the factor of exponential decay. Larger values correspond to more aggressive decay.

LengthPenaltyInput.name: watsonx-orchestrate_LengthPenaltyInput.start_index
LengthPenaltyInput.description: A number of generated tokens after which this should take effect.
